item.title: Wednesday, July 29th, 2026
item.description:
# After my recent dalliance with Vivaldi, the quest for a Brave replacement continues.

On a strange whim I installed the Ecosia browser for the first time since it came out.

It's improved!

Obviously, it's YACB (Yet Another Chromium Browser) but the ad-blocking seems more reliable than DuckDuckGo and it's not got all the bloat of Brave.

It also properly respects the viewport zoom unlike some others I could mention.

item.title: Monday, July 27th, 2026
item.description:
# Kev Quirk links to a couple of posts on the topic of using feed readers vs visiting the actual sites, the first of which has the rather inflammatory title "Your RSS Reader Is Robbing You".

The argument is that if you only read posts in a feed reader then you are not seeing the post as it was intended to be viewed.

I have written a number of posts about this over the past few years. I built /reader with the intent of having an integrated environment where I could reply and send webmentions straight from an item in a feed. Great if the author's site supports webmentions, a bit of a waste if not.

I wrote that "I was unhappy with the homogeneity of seeing everything displayed according to my own style preferences" so built /updates — a view that just gave links to unread items, forcing me to read them in situ. This became more of a notification system than a feed reader.

Previously, I had mentioned that a feed reader "reduces the cognitive load when consuming posts from multiple and varied sources" which echoes the counterpoint from Christian Cleberg that "using RSS allows us to consume many different sites with typography that we prefer".

I've lost count of the times I've debated this with myself, but I'm still using /updates over three years later so suppose that indicates which side of the fence I'm currently on. The good thing is, however, that both views still exist so I can switch between them as I see fit, or as needs dictate.

I was worried if removing the convenience of having everything in one place would mean I read less. I needn't have been. With /updates I have the option to follow individual post links or go to the site homepage where I can go through everything I might not have read.

While I understand that some sites might not be designed to everyone's taste, I feel that we ought to view them at least once in a while to appreciate the work authors are putting into them. Still, it's ultimately a preference thing and that is the beauty of the web.

item.title: Friday, July 24th, 2026
item.description:
# Got the colophon page updated with the latest details. I hadn't touched it for a while and it was sorely out of date. It's still called /specs.

I've deliberately kept the Hello page as /EHLO (Extended Hello - an SMTP command used by servers to request extended features). It's geeky but also cycles back to my old blog from 2003. The tech posts on that site focused on Microsoft Server products, especially SharePoint (which I used to host it, yes SharePoint) and Exchange, so EHLO is a fitting echo.

item.title: Thursday, July 23rd, 2026
item.description:
# I disappeared to the studio for about an hour-and-a-half last night. As is the way when I'm struggling,1 I started something new rather than returning to the couple of works in progress.

I kept to the approach of only having a few things connected at any one time. Last night it was the LM Drum (with the 505 kit), both TD-3s, and the Kobol Expander. I resisted the 'new shiny' temptation of hooking up the Spice and trying to force it into what I was doing. It will, no doubt, become a workhorse in certain situations, but I want to get more familiar with it first.

The Expander has rapidly become a mainstay, finding its way onto almost everything. Luckily, it is versatile enough for things to not get boring or sounding too samey. Maybe that's a little ironic considering everything I make (bar the odd ambient piece) is acid in one form or another.

  1. and I have been stuck on a couple of tracks: one where the idea I had no longer seems to fit; another where I've just not felt like being back in the studio and lost the flow ↩

item.title: Wednesday, July 22nd, 2026
item.description:
# I need to get back in the studio and spent some quality time making music. Working solely in the box is okay, especially with the Launch Control for recording automation, but I get too bogged down.

I find it far more freeing to jam with hardware. In fact, I tend to record a lot of things by playing the different elements or layers live. One at a time, building on what I've done before.

I'll know roughly how things will come together as I almost always do test versions, often recorded live, or build extended loops will all elements to hear what the final result might sound like.

What I want to get into, however, is making fully live recordings – not necessarily dawless, but with only some post processing. What happens is what stays in the final release.

This will need practice. I get too focused on one thing, if I'm tweaking the drums everything else gets ignored. If I'm twisting the knobs on a TD-3 then the drums get boring.

I need to train myself to spread my focus, not get so obsessed with one thing. Actually perform.

# Note to self: I really need to update my colophon after recent changes to the site.
